channel.title: Georgia Public Broadcasting - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Georgia Public Broadcasting (gpb.org)

item.title: The U.S. unexpectedly loses 92,000 jobs, adding to worries about the economy
item.description: The job market showed further signs of weakness last month as employers cut 92,000 jobs. The unemployment rate inched up to 4.4%, from 4.3% in January.

item.title: Atlanta pop-up shop lures hundreds of Harry Styles fans to Beltline for album release
item.description: The British superstar has no plans to perform in Georgia on his 2026 tour, but Atlanta is one of 16 cities chosen to host pop-up merch sales for his new album.

item.title: Poll: A majority of Americans opposes U.S. military action in Iran
item.description: Most Americans disapprove of President Trump's handling of Iran, and a majority sees Iran as either only a minor threat or no threat at all, an NPR/PBS News/Marist poll finds.

item.title: A Jan. 6 rioter pardoned by Trump was sentenced to life in prison for child sex abuse
item.description: Since receiving presidential pardons, dozens of former Capitol rioters have gotten into more legal trouble. In Florida, Andrew Paul Johnson was sentenced to life in prison for child sex abuse.

item.title: 'Dopamine Kids' explains why children crave screens and helps them enjoy life instead
item.description: A mom and science writer offers an operating manual for parents grappling with kids' screen use and cravings for sweets.

item.title: Scientists are discovering that sauna's health benefits aren't all hot air
item.description: It's an age old practice that's having a moment right now. But is there anything to the health claims? Scientists say sauna is more than hot air.

item.title: Bernard LaFayette, Selma voting rights organizer, dies at 85
item.description: Bernard LaFayette, who died Thursday, laid the foundations of the Selma, Alabama, campaign that culminated in the passage of the Voting Rights Act. He was a Freedom Rider and helped found the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee.

item.title: Family, former presidents and a Hall of Famer give Rev. Jesse Jackson a final sendoff
item.description: Several speakers at Jackson's funeral invoked his hallmark catchphrases: "Keep hope alive" and "I am somebody."

item.title: Trump administration's embattled FDA vaccine chief is leaving for the second time
item.description: The FDA's controversial vaccine chief, Dr. Vinay Prasad, is leaving the agency. It's the second time he has abruptly departed following decisions involving the review of vaccinations and specialty drugs.

item.title: Trump looks to turn attention to Western Hemisphere at Americas summit
item.description: President Trump is set to gather with Latin American leaders on Saturday at his Miami-area golf club as his administration looks to turn attention to the Western Hemisphere, at least for a moment.
